concerns.researcher_notes: GEM records P6964 as 'Segment I, operating' of the Yangiyer-Ahangaran Gas Pipeline, paired with P6963 'Segment II, construction' (95 km, dia 1220mm, ConstructionYear=2022). P6964 itself carries NO other data on the sheet -- no length, diameter, capacity, StartYear1, or Owner -- only Status=operating and the shared start/end locations. All four of the wiki-harvested current refs on this row were checked directly and every one describes the NEW 95 km line, not a pre-existing segment: gazeta.uz 2022-12-30 ('Uztransgaz launched construction of a trunk gas pipeline... Yangiyer-Ahangaran, 95 km, dia 1220mm, >47 km of pipe delivered, 6 km installed, commissioning planned Q3 2023') and gazeta.uz 2023-09-30 ('construction continues on another project -- a NEW line [novoi nitki] 95 km long in the Yangiyer-Ahangaran direction') are both explicitly about the new construction project (P6963's story), not confirmation that an older 'Segment I' already operates. The minenergy.uz/1629 press-tour piece cited as the second Status ref is now a soft-404 (HTTP 200 but a client-rendered Next.js 'not found' page, confirmed by direct fetch) -- inaccessible, not a confirmed 404/410, so I am not treating it as deleted, but it currently supports nothing. gem.wiki's own page (read for leads only, never cited) frames Segment I as 'the existing pipeline' but admits 'capacity, length, diameter, and start year are not specified in available documentation' -- i.e. GEM staff never actually sourced a distinct pre-2022 entity, they appear to have inferred one from the framing of the 2022 construction announcements as an 'improvement' project. I searched extensively in Russian for an older/original Yangiyer-Ahangaran line predating the 2022 project (utg.uz history and press pages -- utg.uz/ru/about/history/ 404s; liting.uz / O'ZLITINEFTGAZ institute project lists -- garbled/unreliable OCR text, discounted as a source; ru.wikipedia.org Uztransgaz article -- names only the Ahangaran-Pungan line, 2007-2010, 165 km, through Kamchik pass, with the same Ahangaran compressor station; regnum.ru -- blocked 403) and found nothing that independently names a physically distinct, already-operating 'Yangiyer-Ahangaran' pipeline before the 2022 project. The most economical reading of the evidence is that the Dec-2022 project is the FIRST direct Yangiyer-Ahangaran line, and gas previously reached the Ahangaran hub by other routes (e.g. via the broader trunk network feeding into Ahangaran, from which Ahangaran-Pungan continues into the Fergana valley proper) that were never named 'Yangiyer-Ahangaran'. I could not confirm this either way with a source explicitly stating one-pipeline-not-two, so I am not asserting P6964 = P6963 as a firm duplicate (no source affirmatively describes them as one pipe, which the standing rule requires before flagging duplicate) -- but the existence of a distinct, already-operating Segment I is unconfirmed and should not be presented as sourced fact. No fills are staged for P6964's blank spec fields given this open existence question.
